en: The Blue Great Vajra Yakṣa Rite for Warding Off Ghosts, also known as the Extraordinary Method for Warding Off Ghosts, [performed] at the Śāradvata-cave by the Ācārya Kung-chü. The Root Mudrā:
Join the two hands in *añjali*; bend the two ring fingers (*anāmikā*) and insert them into the palms. Two...
The joints face away from each other.
Use the right *xiangzhi* (index finger) to support the left end of the row,
and use the left *xiangzhi* to support the right end of the row.
Small and wheel-shaped, it destroys all demons and malevolent spirits wherever its seal is applied.
This mantra that subdues all harm is: *phaṭ phaṭ dvināgavi...* [omitted].
1. ...nāya phaṭ 2. ...vasaraṇa phaṭ 3. huṅ mahānināya phaṭ 4. kūpaṇḍa-kañcadanāya phaṭ 5. vaitālī-viśvadanāya phaṭ 6. yakṣa-viśvadanāya phaṭ
Jaya phaṭ | Nṛsiṃha-samarpita-... phaṭ ya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ | Āpad-vighna-praśamana | Tvarita-loka-bhavyaka... ||14||15||16||
16. Ṭa-ṭa-ye (Ṭaṭaye) 17. Rāji-raṃba-ya-te (Rājiraṃbayate) 18. Hūṃ phaṭ ṭaṭaṭa 19. Svāhā. This is also called the Body Mantra.
If there is anyone who wishes to ward off the calamities of the pestilential ghosts that transmit disease,
they should know the symptoms of the illness.
As for the symptoms of the illness:
That person’s body and mind are tormented by feverish distress;
they gradually become emaciated,
or perhaps lose their appetite for food and drink.
At times there is much sleep;
[at other times] there is much suffering that cannot be fully described.
Furthermore, this ghostly illness gradually spreads from person to person in various places—
specifically transmitted among husbands and wives, parents and children, as well as brothers and sisters. For this reason,
people of the time called it the "transmitted corpse ghost" (chuánshī guǐ).
When the Buddha-dharma has become degenerate and diluted,
the kings, ministers, queens, court ladies, and the monks and nuns within the realm— none of whom can be cured even by the most renowned physicians in the world— [will suffer].
Because of being harmed by this [demon],
those of the highest grade become lepers,
while those of the middle grade die from infectious diseases.
The lowest grade results in madness.
For this reason, parents dread [losing] their children, and spouses dread [losing] one another, despite their extraordinary kindness and righteousness.
This pestilence-demon is also called the *Tianmo Luo Nanshiduo* (Heavenly Demon Luo Nanshiduo) ghost.
The *Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha-sūtra* states:
"The symptoms of this ghost-illness resemble those of wind-stroke (*vāta*).
It is also like a madman; the various manifestations of the illness are each like this."
If one does not provide medical treatment within forty-nine days, the patient will certainly die.
When treating this illness,
recite the aforementioned Great Body Mantra twenty-one times while holding white mustard seeds in the right hand.
Recite the aforementioned body-mantra twenty-one times and scatter [it] over the head and face of the patient;
the body of that ghost will shatter into pieces.
If one is afflicted by fire or bitten by a venomous snake, one should recite the aforementioned mantra twenty-one times while striking the person with branches of the *śirīṣa* tree.
By reciting the aforementioned mantra twenty-one times [and applying it], the affliction will immediately be cured. If it is necessary to apply moxibustion, one should treat the patient accordingly.
There are nine locations for moxibustion:
first, the center of the "cross" on the crown of the head;
second, the aperture of the wind-gate (vātadvāra).
Third is the mirror of the navel;
fourth is the heart organ;
fifth is the dantian.
Sixth is the left fengshi (wind market) point;
seventh is the right fengshi point;
eighth is the left pengjiao (pang-jiao) point.
Ninth, regarding the Pengjiao (Pang-jiao) Cavity on the right:

if one does not cauterize the jiao cavity, the person's feet will collapse. When the cavities are generated, [the practitioner] applies the *jin* (bandage/pressing) to the back; at the time of the "cross" (*shizi*) on the great crown of the head...
Recite "HŪṂ PHAṬ" five or seven times.
Possessing the marks of the aggregate of merit of the King of Universal Illumination with a Hundred Lights,
next cauterize the wind-gate.
Recite HŪṂ PHAṬ five or seven times.
Next, when heating the mirror with fire,
recite A Ā I Ī HŪṂ PHAṬ five or seven times.
Next, when cauterizing the heart center,
recite OṂ VAṂ PHAṬ HŪṂ PHAṬ seven times. Next,
when cauterizing the *dantian* (elixir field).
Recite HŪṂ PHAṬ five or seven times. Next,
when cauterizing the left and right wind-blisters (vātārbuda),
recite HAṂ HRAḤ HRĪḤ HRAḤ HŪṂ PHAṬ.
Next, when cauterizing the *péngjiǎo* (pang-chiao) points on the left and right,
recite the syllables VAṂ, ŚAṂ, ṢAṂ, SAṂ, and HŪṂ PHAṬ seven times.
For all the above, empower the site of cauterization with the previously mentioned root mudrā.
This is the place where the *zhiguǐ* (burning demons) and *dōuguǐ* (hooded demons) create obstacles.
If one recites the incantation for the body [of the deity] while performing the "reversal" (*fǎn*) of the various mantras, and applies the ritual with [the hands] extended...
its efficacy will be added to and pre-emptively manifest. One should place aloeswood, white sandalwood, and other such substances into a copper vessel.
Recite the aforementioned mantra twenty-one times.
Consecrate the incense and place it into a decoction of mugwort, willow, and *zhao-liu* (Chinese elm) fruit;
one should then bathe the area where the patient has been cauterized.
The pestilence of transmitted corpses shall cease for one who receives and maintains this seal-dharma,
wearing new and clean garments.
Dwelling in a quiet chamber, [maintaining] the precepts and purifying the mind, one seeks supreme Bodhi above and transforms sentient beings below.
May one recite the "Former Body" mantra three times each day.
After twenty-one days have passed,
one should circumambulate the *dāna* while walking the path,
reciting mantras to empower boiling water, and apply it to the patient.

The practitioner should always use the fundamental mudrā and mantra of the Peacock Vidyārājñī to protect themselves, eliminate all obstacles and difficulties caused by ghosts and spirits, and extinguish evil dreams, miscellaneous dreams, and the like.
To perform the mudrā for summoning the Great Blue Vajra Yakṣa:
join the two hands in *añjali*.
Insert the two index fingers into the palms so that their backs touch, and place them upon the upper joints of the two thumbs.

Furthermore, with two mudrās, point toward the backs of the two deities; opening the [fingers] and moving them to the right, beckon the Honored One. Performing this five times also accomplishes the seal for inviting the five yakṣas.
Recite the aforementioned body-mantra five times, and they will certainly arise and assemble according to the mantra of invitation.
Within the [square] □□□, two deities are enshrined.
As for these two deities:
the first is the Holy Immovable Vidyārāja (Acalanātha), who has six eyes and two wheels.
Second is the Great Vajra Yakṣa of blue color.
Before these two deities, one places a blazing sun disc.
Within the sun disc, one should paint the images of three deities.
The three honored ones are:
first, the Śākyamuni Golden Wheel-Turning Buddha, King of Universal Radiance;
second, the Medicine Master Buddha of Universal Radiance.
Third is the Noble Bodhisattva King of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel (Ārya-Sarvārthasiddhi-Cintāmaṇicakra).
His positions within the Buddha Family, Vajra Family, and Lotus Family are as shown in the diagram below.
Next, fashion three images of demons and place them within a bronze gong filled with oil.
Recite the mantra of the Holy Immovable Tathāgata one hundred and eight times.

Boil the three effigies of the demons and perform homa in the fire-pit for twenty-one nights. If there is still no sign of efficacy, practice this for twenty-one days (three weeks), and so forth. At that time, the three demons will manifest their forms; within the ashes, there will be the letter *Aṃ*.
The syllable *A* transforms into the tranquil and holy Immovable Lord (Acalanātha).

This is called the "Return of the Three Ghosts" and the Abiding in the Great Boundary of the Unmoving True Suchness (*tathatā*). It is like the Dharma of the Golden Wheel of Mahāvairocana. If there are kings who diligently practice this Dharma, they shall be free from illness, enjoy long life, and their lands shall be peaceful, stable, and abundant. For those who uphold this Dharma, its sublime efficacy is immeasurable. [Regarding] the path of disease... if one recites this mantra of the Vidyārāja one thousand eight hundred times, at that very moment—
Manifesting his form-body to empower the practitioner:
if one wishes to eliminate the afflictions and obstacles caused by malevolent spirits and demons,
one should face this blue Vajra and recite [the mantra] seven hundred times.
Furthermore, for those whom he manifests as a ghost or spirit to protect,
if one wishes to eliminate seasonal epidemics or diseases caused by celestial influences, one should strike the patient with branches of the *śirīṣa* tree, and they will immediately be cured.

This brief explanation of the minor [rite] for the fulfillment of virtuous vows is as described in the *Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha-sūtra*. This extraordinary method for exorcising demons is a most secret among secrets.

It is constantly empowered and protected by the fifteen seals (*mudrā*) of the Fire Realm; because it exists within the Great Sun’s Golden Wheel Empowerment Method (*Vairocana-suvarṇacakra-abhiṣeka-vidhi*), it is not worn [as a crest]. [The deity] is blue in color, possesses three eyes and four arms, and is a Vajra-being.
His face is that of a great wrathful deity, with bared fangs and three eyes protruding upward; he has a most terrifying appearance.
Upon his head he wears a skull, his hair bristles upward, and a great serpent of [specific] color coils around his crown.
Regarding the four-armed form:
the first left hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*);
the first right hand grasps a noose (*pāśa*); [the second right hand] holds a great sword (*mahā-khaḍga*).
The right second hand holds a golden wheel; the two shoulders are adorned with [ornaments], and he wears a necklace made of skulls and a lower garment of tiger skin.
Furthermore, his left and right feet each trample upon a ghost.
The foot-dragging demons on the left and right have forms like skeletal corpses.

This Great Vajra Yakṣa, with extreme wrath, is accompanied by the four great yakṣas and their retinues; the yellow and red yakṣas all hold great swords, while the blue and black yakṣas wield tridents.
The feet and claws of these four great yakṣas are all long and sharp like swords;
each leads a retinue of eighty thousand yakṣas to protect and sustain all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa in the south.
This concludes the maṇḍala.
At the time of a solar or lunar eclipse,
one should immediately construct a small altar and adorn this maṇḍala.

According to one's capacity, prepare the food and drink... [omitted] ...and wait until the days and months are again complete. When those who eat it... [omitted] ...if there are those who practice... [omitted] ...they shall attain the six... [omitted] ...dharmas, and there will be no further rebirth. To clarify the altar, there are thirteen items: first, food and drink; second, a pure mirror; third, the four great knives; fourth, four arrows; fifth, five-colored threads.
These are the ritual implements for the royal palace.
Next, the ritual implements for protection [and other purposes] follow the general ritual protocols for offerings.

Because they bring about the swift attainment and realization of every single accomplishment—such as pacification (*śānti*), endearment (*vaśīkaraṇa*), official rank, fortune, and subjugation (*abhicāra*)—[they are essential].
In the final age, foolish people will turn their backs on this Dharma.

The Tripiṭaka Master who translated the scriptures kept it deeply secret and did not transmit it; only after the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) of the *Mahāvairocana-sūtra* was this text transmitted. He praised these four lines as follows:

HŪṂ HŪṂ VAJRAYAKṢARĀJA NAMAḤ STUTE | APRATIHATA NAMAḤ SARVAMĀRAPAŚAVIMOCANE STUTE | VAJRA-JVALA-BHRŪṄAṂ NAMAḤ STUTE | Bowing my head, I pay homage to the Blue Great Vajra Yakṣa Vidyārāja. This secret praise must not be transmitted to the unworthy.
[Great Vajra] ... [separately] bestow it at another time.
Because all [the treasures] within the treasury possess various riches, this is called *siddhi* ...
[on the day of the ghost-mara] perform the pouring out ... show the seal-mark as before, like the wheel-seal.
However, [I] shall open [the gate of] consciousness and point toward the secret within secrets;
furthermore, it shall not be transmitted to anyone other than these two persons.
As for the phrase "three ghost-forms": [it refers to...]
The first are human ghosts,
such as those that assume the form of a corpse.
The second are celestial ghosts.
It takes the form of an owl.
This refers to the celestial foxes. Thirdly, there are the terrestrial ghosts, which take the form of earth-foxes.
They are also called epilepsy-demons (*apasmāra-graha*).

Abiding with a mind of great valor within the [mandala], one should recite the mantra of the Immovable Fire Realm (*Acala-jvālā-dhātu*) one hundred times. Once the three images of the demons have been boiled, they will enter the samādhi of the Immovable Honored One’s Fire. One should remain constantly in this state; for the details of the visualization, consult the ritual manual (*vidhi*).
Regarding the two illnesses of ghosts and demons, these must be cured through the power of deep contemplative practice and the power of mantras; only then will they be healed.
As for karmic illnesses, one must rely on internal meditative power and external repentance; only then can they be cured.

When the multitude are governed, they do not [attain]... if one well grasps their intent, one must not wield a blade or handle a weapon to harm oneself... The *Shenqiu Changsheng Jing* (Scripture on Seeking Longevity) says: "The 'drum' of turbidity resides in the darkness of the eyes; the foul odor of the mouth causes teeth to fall out.

The 'drum-substance' resides within the abdomen, striking and damaging the person's internal organs, causing the vital breath (*qi*) to diminish. One must avoid the likes and dislikes of others and dare not eat living beings. When the 'drum' resides in the feet, it obstructs and agitates the five essences, causing them to leap and stir uncontrollably. If the spirit is harmed, longevity will be cut short. On the first day of the month of Geng, the Heavenly Emperor records the sins of men; when these transgressions sever one’s register of life, he desires that death come swiftly so that the soul enters the three springs. At that time...

This is called the calamity of ghosts afflicting humans, causing heart pain, convulsions, and various demonic afflictions that are transmitted to descendants, siblings, and sisters. This includes the "transmitted corpse" (*chuánshī*) and "reconnecting the bones" (*fùlián gǔ*) diseases; there are also cases where an entire clan dies out without anyone being able to fathom the cause. Recently, such cases have become increasingly frequent, with the more severe instances resulting in death within no more than a few months.

Therefore, people fear it most intensely; fathers and sons sever their kinship, and husbands and wives break their bonds of righteousness. [This is] the true nature of illness as found in the original text of the sutra.
As for those who are exhausted by the corpse, they may practice it.

Furthermore, when practicing correct contemplation, if the practitioner harbors wrong thoughts during seated meditation, Māra will manifest various garments, food, drink, and assorted objects of the seven treasures;
the practitioner then accepts these visions, which enter the mind and become a source of affliction.
This text on the difficulty of treating this illness was transcribed from the Imperial manuscript in the □□ room on the twenty-sixth day of the □□ month. Recorded by Gyeong-bam.
On the eighteenth day of the first month of the second year of Shōan,
I received the oral transmission from the quarters of Ajari Jōjō no Suke.
Keikan recorded this.
On the eleventh day of the first month of the second year of Ken’ei,
based on the original manuscript from Gwetchirinbō,
copied by Kumo no Kuni.
On the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month in the second year of the Jōkū era,
this was transcribed by Hōren of Go-hōshō.
This ritual manual is a secret text brought back from the Mitsui lineage.
Regarding this, the person after [Master] Ao was named Jia; this is recorded in the *Xiangjue ji*.
